Pure crystals of copper sulphate can be obtained by crystallisation of saturated solution of impure Bazzar copper sulphate. The solution which can dissolve no more solute at a given temperature is called saturated solution at that temperature. Filter the solution and collect the filtrate in a basin. The filfrate is saturated solution at room temperature.
Place the basin containing the filtrate over the sand bath. Evaporate it to the crystallisation point. During evaporation, sår the solution with a glass rod to avoid the crust formation.
After evaporating for some time, introduce few drops of the evaporated solution on the outer wall of a test tube containing cold water with the help of a glass rod.

When the solution attains the crystallisation point, tiny crystals (crust) are seen deposited on the wall of the test tube immediately after the removal of the glass rod from the contact of the test tube.
When the crystallisation point is reached, stop heating the solution immediately.
Make the porcelain basin float on the water taken in a large beaker or water trough.
The liquid begins to cool. Gradually, the salt will crystallize out of the solution.

Take out the crystals from the basin on a filter paper carefully without disturbing their shapes and sizes.

Object: TO OBTAIN COMMON SALT BY NEUTRALIZATION

Common salt can be obtained by neutralisation of bench hydrochloric acid with bench sodium hydroxide. It is obtained in dry and solid state by evaporating its aqueous solution. Neutralisation can be defined as the process in which an acid and a base react to give salt and water.
Evaporation can be defined as the process of conversion of a liquid into its vapour form.
